question: When can a New York State agency run an SDVOB set-aside procurement?
answer: A New York State agency may conduct an SDVOB set-aside procurement at any time after considering a Preferred Source, without having to comply with the order of priority for selecting a procurement method. This is stated in the New York State Procurement Guidelines, which note that an agency may conduct an SDVOB set-aside procurement at any time after considering a Preferred Source. The guidelines also indicate that SDVOB set-asides are part of the order of purchasing priority, specifically at the second and third levels.
